findings.reality: Two competing store authorities exist and one is not thread-safe. python/synapse/memory/store.py:1517 get_synapse_memory() is an unlocked check-then-create; two threads construct two SynapseMemory objects, one orphaned while holding a Moneta handle on the same storage dir. python/synapse/memory/ledger.py:424 does the same job correctly under _MONETA_LOCK, keyed by abspath(ledger_dir()), closing the prior handle.
findings.consequence: The submitted fix (a singleton inside MemoryPort) adds a THIRD authority in a module nothing calls, and leaves both real ones untouched.

findings.claim: approval_token is a manual human-approval gate to delete under the zero-LLM law
findings.reality: It is a plan-binding CAS nonce. A dry-run computes a consolidation plan and hashes it; apply refuses unless the caller returns the token for THAT plan (python/synapse/memory/consolidation.py:343-351).
findings.consequence: Removing it deletes optimistic-concurrency control from the only destructive memory operation in the product. Rename it; do not remove it.
